text:
Ashley: FYI I'm seeing the GPU nodepool oscillate this morning — CA adds a 4-node gpu-pool, then within ~6m scale-down removes them, then pods go Pending again and loop.

Samir: Any metrics or logs we can correlate? RPS or queue spikes?

Ashley: Prometheus shows external metric 'service_queue_depth{team="realtime"}' jumping from ~10 to ~80 in short bursts. HPA is configured to use that external metric (target avg=25) plus a CPU target at 60%. HPA has no stabilization window configured (we're on HPA v2 metrics).

Lee: Ouch — GPU nodes take ~4–6 minutes to be Ready (driver install + CUDA init). CA will see pods Pending for a few minutes; if scale-down window is short it can remove nodes before pods become Ready. We also have some preemptible GPUs in that pool so evictions are happening.

Maria: VPA recommender has been issuing "increase" recommendations, and our VPA is currently in 'auto' mode for that deployment — it has been triggering restarts that line up with the HPA spikes. Classic feedback loop.

devops-bot: autoscaler.log: [2024-05-11T08:12:03Z] cluster-autoscaler: nodegroup gpu-pool scaled 0 -> 4 (reason: 6 pending pods). [2024-05-11T08:18:45Z] cluster-autoscaler: scale-down: removed 2 nodes (utilization 0.05).

Samir: A few concrete mitigations we should consider: 
- Use HPA 'behavior' with stabilizationWindowSeconds and scaleDown/scaleUp limits so short bursts don't flip counts.
- Tweak CA flags: --scale-down-unneeded-time and --scale-down-delay-after-add to be >= node warmup time.
- Add a tiny always-on warm nodepool (1 node) in the GPU pool to avoid cold starts.

Ashley: Also the external metrics adapter is feeding the raw queue_depth (per-scrape). We should add a Prometheus recording rule to smooth it (e.g., avg_over_time 60s) and point HPA at that rule to ignore microbursts.

Lee: Agree. Additionally: set VPA mode to 'recommend' for the realtime deployment. VPA restarts + HPA scale events create thrash. For GPU workloads we should avoid 'auto' unless validated.

Maria: We can also change HPA to a composite approach: prefer 'rps_per_pod' or 'inflight_requests' and keep 'minReplicas' to 2 so we never scale to zero. Consider switching the node pool off preemptible for critical instances or set preemptionPolicy to 'Never' if cloud provider supports it.

Samir: Small infra trick: add a startupProbe/readinessProbe that checks CUDA driver and nvidia-device-plugin readiness so pods don't appear unhealthy while drivers initialize. That prevents early rescheduling.

Ashley: Action items: 
1) Samir: create a recording rule to smooth queue_depth and open a PR updating HPA to use behavior.stabilizationWindowSeconds=120 and scaleDownPolicy limits.
2) Lee: flip VPA to 'recommend' for the realtime deploy and add note in the playbook.
3) Infra: create 1-node "gpu-warm" nodepool (non-preemptible) and adjust CA flags: --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m --scale-down-delay-after-add=15m.
4) Maria: add Grafana alert for node add/remove rate >3 in 30m and for sudden queue_depth spikes.

Maria: +1 on all. Let's monitor and reconvene after 6 hours.

Ashley: I'll watch the next deploy window and post updates here. Thanks team :thumbsup:
